notes.A: Cuts and bottles line the counter against brick, but the hanging carcass is cropped.
notes.B: The pitcher and barrel shelves read clearly, but the cropped meat barely identifies the shop.
notes.C: Hanging meat and counter goods establish the trade, but the bright jar steals focus.
notes.D: Hanging cuts, counter, shelves, and aisle read together, though the nearest carcass hides some stock.
notes.E: Hanging cuts and the tiled aisle are visible, but a huge foreground carcass blocks shelving.
notes.F: The aisle explains the layout, but the long shelf crowds the meat counter.
notes.G: The floor and endcap show the layout, but the butcher counter recedes into shadow.
notes.H: The shelf top dominates, pushing the meat counter and hanging cuts to the right edge.

market_hall.best: The diagonal view ties hanging cuts, the long sales counter, stocked shelves, and the checkerboard aisle into one readable scene.
market_hall.lacks: The dim, even lighting gives the meat display little emphasis, so the market’s defining feature blends into the surrounding stock.
market_hall.fix: Add one warm overhead light that picks out the hanging cuts and the counter directly beneath them.

blind_name.name: Butcher’s stall
blind_name.why: Skinned carcasses hang above a wooden counter, with stocked shelves and crates behind it.
blind_name.odd: The bottle labels are too pixelated to read.
